questions.statement:
The European Island That Swaps Nationality Twice a Year
Sophie-May Williams
01
“There are no pheasants __ Pheasant Island,” complained the French author Victor Hugo
02 __ 1843. Calm down, Mr. Hugo. The lack __ game birds is the least interesting thing __ the
03 place. Less than 200 meters long and 40 meters wide, this tiny stretch of land on the Bidasoa
04 River between France and Spain boasts something truly unique: it changes nationality every six
05 months.
06
Let’s backtrack a bit. Pheasant Island is uninhabited, briefly home to migratory birds and
07 wild animals, and lush with greenery. Sunshine is permanent, thanks to the year-long subtropical
08 climate. The only structure is a 19th-century monolith that shares both Spanish and French
09 inscriptions, a symbol of peace between the two nations. But there’s more to this geopolitical
10 anomaly than meets the eye. From February 1 to July 31, it’s under Spanish rule. Then, from
11 August 1 to January 31, it belongs to France.
12
Despite adhering to such a curious concept, few people have heard of the island. Or what
13 it stands for. Back in 1659, it served as the signing location for the Treaty of the Pyrenees. This
14 was a significant peace treaty between Louis XIV of France and Philip IV of Spain, as it ended
15 the 30-year Franco-Spanish War. Remember the tomb-like monolith from earlier? It was erected
16 centuries later to commemorate this very meeting. In simple terms, it gave each nation the
17 chance to govern the humanless island. Sharing is caring, after all. The occasion was so
18 momentous that a year later, French King Louis XIV married the daughter of King Philip IV, Maria
19 Theresa of Spain, in the exact spot where the treaty was signed. Wooden bridges were erected
20 so royal entourages could pass through in barges and carriages, and paintings were
21 commissioned to immortalize the event.
22
These days, general access to Pheasant Island is prohibited. The only time you might be
23 able to set

Which verb tense is mainly used throughout the second paragraph, and why is it used?

options.text: Simple present, because it describes facts about the island — things that will probably not change in the near future.
Present perfect, because the present facts described are consequences of actions that happened in the past.
Simple past, because the past events have a clear time reference.
Simple present, because the events described are not permanent, but temporary.
Present perfect, because the stated events do not have a past time reference.

questions.explanation: O simple present descreve fatos, características e estados habituais ou relativamente estáveis da ilha. O present perfect liga passado e presente, enquanto o simple past situa fatos concluídos; não se trata de acontecimentos apenas temporários.

questions.statement:
The Benefits of Board Games for Students
01
Board games challenge students to think critically, weigh their options, and adapt strategies
02 in real time. Unlike passive learning, games like Rush Hour require active decision-making where
03 each move has consequences. When ____ (calculate) risks in Chess or ____ (predict) an
04 opponent’s next move in Onitama, students strengthen skills such as strategic planning, logical
05 reasoning, and problem-solving. These abilities not only enhance academic performance but also
06 prepare them for real-world challenges requiring quick thinking and adaptability.
07
Many games also reinforce academic skills in a fun, low-pressure way. Unlike traditional
08 worksheets or drills, games like Codenames, Sushi Go Party!, and Letter Tycoon provide
09 hands-on learning experiences that encourage students to think critically. Whether they are
10 calculating scores, forming words, or recognizing patterns, students absorb key math and literacy
11 concepts. Because board games naturally reward effort and strategy, they help students build
12 confidence in these areas, making them more likely to approach academic challenges with a
13 positive mindset.
14
Losing a game can be frustrating, but it also presents a valuable lesson in resilience and
15 emotional regulation. Options like Sorry!, Forbidden Island, and Karuba help students develop a
16 growth mindset, teaching them how to handle setbacks, adapt strategies, and persist through
17 challenges. These experiences translate directly into better emotional resilience in school and
18 everyday life.
19
With constant digital distractions, sustained attention has become a valuable skill. Board
20 games nurture focus by requiring players to plan ahead and remain attentive throughout the
21 game. Unlike fast-paced video games that often shorten attention spans, board games reward
22 concentration and patience. For students with attention challenges, games like Go (Baduk) can
23 be particularly

Mark the alternative that fills in, correctly and respectively, the blanks in the first paragraph.
questions.explanation: Após “When”, o texto usa orações reduzidas de valor temporal: “calculating risks” e “predicting an opponent’s next move”. As formas em -ing mantêm paralelismo e exprimem ações em curso; infinitivos, formas finitas e futuros não se ajustam à construção.

questions.statement:
The secret history of Stonehenge
By James Owens
01
Stonehenge, located in southern England, ranks among the world’s most iconic
02 archaeological sites and one of its greatest enigmas. The megalithic stone circle on Salisbury
03 Plain inspires awe and fascination — but also intense debate some 4,600 years after it was built
04 by ancient Britons who left no written record.
05
The monument’s mysterious past has spawned countless tales and theories. According to
06 folklore, Stonehenge was created ___ Merlin, the wizard of Arthurian legend, who magically
07 transported the massive stones ___ Ireland, where giants had assembled them.
08
Another legend says invading Danes put the stones up, and another theory says they were
09 the ruins of a Roman temple. Modern-day interpretations are no less colorful. Some argue that
10 Stonehenge is a spacecraft landing area for aliens, and even more say it’s a giant fertility symbol
11 in the shape of female genitalia.
12
Archaeological investigation of the site dates back to the 1660s, when it was first surveyed
13 by antiquarian John Aubrey. He wrongly credited Stonehenge to the much later Celts, believing
14 it to be a religious center presided over by Druid priests.
15
Centuries of fieldwork since show the Neolithic monument, now a UNESCO World Heritage
16 site, was more than a millennium in the making. It started out 5,000 years ago as a circular
17 earthen bank and ditch, in a larger area of burial mounds.
18
Modern debate over the monument’s meaning has two main camps: those who see it as a
19 holy site, and others who believe it represents a scientific observatory.
20
Both camps base their theories on the site’s celestial influence. They point to alignments to
21 the sun and moon as evidence of rituals linked to the changing seasons and
22 the summer and winter solstices.
23

24 came to be healed. This idea revolves around the smaller blue

Considering the informal case, which word can replace the word “who” in “Merlin is the wizard who magically transported the massive stones”?
questions.explanation: Em oração relativa restritiva referente a pessoa, “that” pode substituir informalmente “who” quando exerce função de sujeito. “Whom” é forma objetiva; “whose” indica posse, “when” tempo e “him” não é pronome relativo.

questions.statement:
California is Free of Drought for The First Time in 25 Years
By Clara Harter
01
After experiencing one of the wettest holiday seasons on record, California hit a major
02 milestone this week — having zero areas of abnormal dryness for the first time in 25 years. The
03 data, collected by the U.S. Drought Monitor, is a welcome nugget of news for Golden State*
04 residents, who in the last 15 years alone have lived through two of the worst droughts on record,
05 the worst wildfire seasons on record, and the most destructive wildfires ever. Right now, the
06 wildfire risk across California is “about as close to zero as it ever gets,” and there is likely no
07 need to worry about the state’s water supply for the rest of the year, said UC climate scientist
08 Daniel Swain. Currently, 14 of the state’s 17 major water supply reservoirs are at 70% or more
09 capacity, according to the California Department of Water Resources.
10
California’s last drought lasted more than 1,300 days, from February 2020 to October 2023,
11 at which point just 0.7% of the state remained abnormally dry, thanks to a series of winter
12 atmospheric rivers that showered the Golden State with rain. Before that, California was in a
13 severe drought from 2012 through 2016. But the last time 0% of the California map had any
14 level of abnormally dry or drought conditions was all the way back in December 2000. In recent
15 weeks, a series of powerful winter storms and atmospheric rivers have swept across California,
16 dumping heavy rain that soaked soils, filled reservoirs, and left much of the state unusually wet
17 for this time of year. “This is certainly a less destructive winter weather than last year was,”
18 Swain said. He noted, however, that “as we move forward, we do expect to be dealing with
19 increasingly extreme [weather] swings.”
20

21 intense droughts and more intense episodes of rainfall. This is be

It quantifies the uncountable noun “news”. III. It refers to an official or technical report released by authorities. Which ones are correct?
questions.explanation: Em “a nugget of news”, nugget tem sentido figurado de pequena porção ou informação, permitindo individualizar o substantivo incontável news. Não significa literalmente uma pepita mineral nesse contexto e tampouco designa um relatório oficial ou técnico.

questions.statement:
California is Free of Drought for The First Time in 25 Years
By Clara Harter
01
After experiencing one of the wettest holiday seasons on record, California hit a major
02 milestone this week — having zero areas of abnormal dryness for the first time in 25 years. The
03 data, collected by the U.S. Drought Monitor, is a welcome nugget of news for Golden State*
04 residents, who in the last 15 years alone have lived through two of the worst droughts on record,
05 the worst wildfire seasons on record, and the most destructive wildfires ever. Right now, the
06 wildfire risk across California is “about as close to zero as it ever gets,” and there is likely no
07 need to worry about the state’s water supply for the rest of the year, said UC climate scientist
08 Daniel Swain. Currently, 14 of the state’s 17 major water supply reservoirs are at 70% or more
09 capacity, according to the California Department of Water Resources.
10
California’s last drought lasted more than 1,300 days, from February 2020 to October 2023,
11 at which point just 0.7% of the state remained abnormally dry, thanks to a series of winter
12 atmospheric rivers that showered the Golden State with rain. Before that, California was in a
13 severe drought from 2012 through 2016. But the last time 0% of the California map had any
14 level of abnormally dry or drought conditions was all the way back in December 2000. In recent
15 weeks, a series of powerful winter storms and atmospheric rivers have swept across California,
16 dumping heavy rain that soaked soils, filled reservoirs, and left much of the state unusually wet
17 for this time of year. “This is certainly a less destructive winter weather than last year was,”
18 Swain said. He noted, however, that “as we move forward, we do expect to be dealing with
19 increasingly extreme [weather] swings.”
20
Though it may seem counterintuitive, climate change is forecast to lead to both more
21 intense droughts and more intense episodes of rainfall. This is be

Which of the sentences below presents an example of a superlative structure?

options.text: Climate change is forecast to lead to both more intense droughts and more intense episodes of rainfall.
A warmer atmosphere pulls more moisture out of soils and plants.
At the same time, it holds more water vapor, which is then released in fewer rainstorms.
We actually are likely to see wider swings between extremely wet conditions and extremely dry conditions.
Southern California experienced one of the driest periods on record in the fall and winter of 2024.

questions.explanation: A construção “one of the driest periods” contém o superlativo driest, formado com o sufixo -est, e situa um período entre os mais secos. Nas demais frases, more, wider ou extremely express comparação ou intensidade, não uma estrutura superlativa.

The underlined word “extremely” in “we actually are likely to see wider swings between extremely wet conditions” (l. 26) is an
questions.explanation: Extremely é advérbio de intensidade que modifica o adjetivo wet, compondo o grupo “extremely wet conditions”. Não caracteriza diretamente o substantivo conditions nem modifica verbo ou outro advérbio; sua função é intensificar a qualidade expressa pelo adjetivo.

The underlined word “should” in “Fortunately, California should be clear of water supply risks” (l. 37) expresses a:

options.text: Rule to be followed by the state of California.
Wish for something to happen or become true.

questions.explanation: Em “California should be clear of water supply risks”, should exprime expectativa provável inferida das condições descritas, e não obrigação ou conselho. Também não é simples desejo: a previsão se apoia no quadro favorável de reservatórios e chuvas apresentado no texto.

Mark the INCORRECT statement about the excerpt “atmospheric rivers have swept across California” (l. 15).

options.text: It is a present perfect tense sentence.
Its structure contains a subject, an auxiliary verb, a past particle main verb, and a complement.
This verb tense never describes finished events. Instead, it is used for actions occurring at the present moment or within the current time frame.
The interrogative version of this sentence, in the same verb tense, is “Have atmospheric rivers swept across California?”.
The excerpt is in the active voice, not the passive.

questions.explanation: “Have swept” está no present perfect: auxiliar have mais particípio swept, em voz ativa, com sujeito atmospheric rivers. A pergunta inverte auxiliar e sujeito. É incorreto dizer que esse tempo nunca descreve eventos concluídos: ele pode indicar fatos passados relevantes no presente.

questions.statement: In the excerpt “Meanwhile, his double-panel […] was painted around the same time, though exactly when is unclear”, the underlined words “Meanwhile” and “though” express, respectively:
questions.explanation: Meanwhile estabelece relação temporal, indicando simultaneidade ou o período em que outro fato ocorre. Though introduz concessão ou contraste entre ideias. As demais combinações atribuem aos conectores sentidos de causa, condição, finalidade ou resultado.
questions.section: 2. Tempos verbais, aspecto e sequência temporal

questions.statement: In the excerpt “Four Renaissance paintings of ‘extraordinary value’ have been stolen from a museum in Sicily”, what is the correct classification and description of the underlined verb phrase “have been stolen”?

options.text: Simple past in the passive voice – describes an action completed at a specific time in the past.
Present perfect in the active voice – emphasizes the agent responsible for the action.
Past perfect in the passive voice – describes an action that occurred before another past event.
Present perfect in the passive voice – emphasizes a past action with relevance to the present.
Present continuous in the passive voice – indicates an action occurring at the moment of speaking.

questions.explanation: Have been stolen combina o auxiliar have, o particípio been e o particípio stolen: é present perfect na voz passiva. Expressa ação passada com repercussão presente e põe em foco as pinturas, não o agente do furto.

questions.statement: According to the excerpt taken from the text “Antonello da Messina was a 15th Century painter born and raised on Sicily, who would go on to become one of the early Renaissance period’s master painters,” mark the correct statement regarding the use of the word “who” in the excerpt.

options.text: It refers to Antonello da Messina and adds extra information about his career.
It refers to Sicily, pointing out the location where the artist worked.
It could be correctly replaced by the pronoun “that” without any grammatical error.
It can be replaced by “which” because it refers to the 15th Century.
It is used to identify the specific painter being referred to in the sentence.

questions.explanation: Who retoma o pintor Antonello da Messina e introduz oração relativa explicativa sobre sua trajetória. Não retoma lugar ou período; por ser uma oração não restritiva, separada por vírgula, não admite a troca por that.
